Major rehabilitation work, superstructure, and/or total bridge replacement. This project is being completed in conjunction with TIPID 1415, Rt 5, Lambert Lind Hwy (Mayfield Ave to I-95).

Preservation - work to extend the useful service life of the structure, which may include joint replacement, bridge washing, zone painting, deck repairs, minimum to moderate concrete or steel superstructure repairs, moderate substructure repairs, culvert repairs and other incidentals.

Preservation - work to extend the useful service life of the structure, which may include joint replacement, bridge washing, zone painting, deck repairs, minimum to moderate conrete or steel superstructure repairs, moderate substructure repairs, culvert repairs and other incidentals.

Safety Improvements to Pontiac Avenue, Sockanosset Cross Road, and the Route 37 on- and off-ramps, including the introduction of dual left-turn lanes northbound onto Sockanosset Cross Road, widening of the Route 37 West off-ramp onto Pontiac Avenue (TIP ID 6770, Bridge #126401), and signal improvements to improve traffic flow.

This line item involves the non-Federal Transit Administration funding used for the construction of the 6/10 Interchange and associated bridges to bring this section of roadway into a state of good repair.
This line item will support design and development of a potential future project to address the "missing move" between Route 4 and I-95.

This project involves the construction of a park including constructing walkways, a gathering area, and a bituminous three spot parking lot; furnishing and installing trees, landscaping and all other incidentals necessary. The park was originally a part of a stormwater mitigation action for Bridge 055001. The lot where the park is to be constructed is 20 Division Street in Pawtucket, just East of the Division Street Bridge.

projects.notes: Small (a few dozen) set of proposed long-range plan projects from RI Statewide Planning; ProjStatus (e.g. Planning), FundStatus and STIPYr (e.g. 'FY 22 - 31') tie some to the current STIP. Cost is mostly blank. Supplementary only.

parcels_counties.notes: City of Cranston parcels in RIGIS standard format joined to the assessor CAMA extract (tax roll year in CAMAExtract_TaxRollYear). Rhode Island has no county government; parcels are kept by the 39 cities and towns.

summary: Projects: only an outdated STIP map service (FFY2018-2027, 2020 amendment) and a small LRTP proposed-projects layer were found; no current RIDOT planned-projects GIS service was verified. Parcels: no statewide owner layer (RIGIS publishes none; parcels are municipal, many on vendor viewers without open services); only Cranston's city layer with owner and mailing address was verified, Providence was not found.
